# Unit 1 practice paper — answers and marking guidance

48 marks. Classroom draft. Accept equivalent correct answers. Award points only for the stated evidence; avoid double-crediting the same point. Teacher reviews diagram symbols and alternative explanations. This is not grade calibration.

## Q1 (3 marks)

1 mark: 1000011 or 01000011. 1: hexadecimal 43. 1: a code point identifies a character; byte length depends on encoding, so it is not always one byte.

## Q2 (4 marks)

1: remainder 3. 1: Boolean result True. 1: ((not False) and False) or True, with NOT before AND before OR. 1: = assigns; == compares.

## Q3 (5 marks)

1: at i=1, best remains 0. 1: at i=2, best remains 0 because 6 > 6 is false. 1: index 0 and maximum 6. 1: sum 10. 1: check non-empty before accessing element zero; define an empty result. A correct alternative trace layout earns credit.

## Q4 (4 marks)

1: valid function header with the three parameters. 1: correctly grouped return expression. 1: age/has_permission/is_escorted are parameters; 15/True/False are arguments. 1: False.

## Q5 (4 marks)

1: 99 accepted. 1: 100 accepted. 1: 101 rejected. 1: text such as abc or 2.5 rejected as integer input. Award each point only when the expected outcome accompanies the input.

## Q6 (4 marks)

1: w replaces the earlier data. 1: use a to retain and append, with a newline record separator. 1: a with block closes the file when the block exits. 1: sum 5 after reading the two records; assume valid integer lines.

## Q7 (4 marks)

1: it fails an agreed recovery requirement despite correct calculation. 1: organiser enters invalid text then a valid quantity and continues without restarting. 1: isolated calculation call with known input and expected return. 1: evidence-based reflection about the development process and a future change, such as earlier validation testing.

## Q8 (3 marks)

1: open source requires licence rights to use, modify and redistribute, not just visibility. 1: plagiarism concerns misrepresenting authorship; acknowledgement does not independently grant permission. 1: exact licence/permission and conditions, or creator/source/version with an explanation of its use.

## Q9 (4 marks)

1 each: Application — HTTPS/web service; Transport — TCP/ordered stream; Internet — IP/addressing and routing; Network — Ethernet or Wi-Fi/local frames. Both layer and role/example are required for each mark.

## Q10 (3 marks)

1: IPv4 32 bits versus IPv6 128 bits (IPv6 has a larger address space). 1: no, their /24 network addresses differ. 1: the mask identifies the network portion used in that comparison.

## Q11 (6 marks)

1: switch with wired PCs and local server. 1: access point links wireless clients to the LAN. 1: router and appropriate provider/modem connection, with correctly connected course symbols. 1: coherent unique addresses/masks and firewall outside trusted network without IP label. 1: justified medium, such as UTP for fixed nearby PCs or fibre for a suitably described long link. 1: evidence-based performance choice, such as investigating wireless airtime/placement rather than assuming a faster switch fixes everything. Teacher visually checks symbol fidelity; alternative coherent layouts can earn credit.

## Q12 (4 marks)

1: firewall permits/blocks traffic according to rules. 1: OS authentication, permissions or updates with a threat explanation. 1: broadcasts consume capacity/processing within the broadcast domain. 1: contention/collisions on shared media consume time; modern full-duplex switched Ethernet avoids old half-duplex collision behaviour.
